correctness.rationale: In (F_2^d;R,0), ternary R and equality atoms are determined by vanishing sums of support at most three. For k>=4, preserve proper-subset (<k) linear dependencies among k pebbles: after one relocation, remaining k-1 vectors have exactly matching spans, and an outside response exists unless rank k-1, where replacing by their total sum only changes a full-support k-dependency invisible to all atoms. This is a back-and-forth for every round when both d,e>=k-1. For k<=3 preserve all dependencies with dimensions >=k. Finite-variable nested accumulator formulas express m-vector independence using m+1 symbol names for m>=3, and special widths 1,2,3 distinguish smaller ranks. Thus dimensions truncated at tau(k)=k (k<=3), k-1 (k>=4) exactly classify FO^k theories. Independently checked rank boundary: any five vectors in F2^4 are dependent, while a five-element basis of F2^5 has no nonempty zero-sum subset. This is a boundary check, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: A 2007 Gomaa dissertation and 2008 conference text claim unconditionally that five variables distinguish any two nonisomorphic finite abelian groups in the same ternary relational language. Its proof applies sets of cyclic component orders, losing multiplicity: (F2)^4 and (F2)^5 share component-order set {2} despite different dimension. The submitted five-variable counterexample and all-k truncation theorem contradict that specific earlier assertion rather than being a corollary. Earlier finite-round and two-variable classifications in Resultary concern fixed quantifier depth or variation across primes, not the full dimension-by-width law at unrestricted quantifier depth. The related 2010 journal full article was not obtained, so characterization of its detailed proof remains limited.
